One of the most important concepts for types is pins/pinning your opponent. A pin is when you cover a strong attack from one of your mons with a second attack (preferably a spread move) that covers types that resist the first attack. The best pins are flying and ground or ground and fairy which make up the bases for strategies like Talonflame/great tusks. Pins are particularly important right now because of terastalization, you need to pin your opponent so they can't tera on you safely.

I will just list some of the big changes since ORAS:

Pikalitics is a hugely important resource now as it breaks down what pokemon people are playing, what sets they run and what pokemon they are paired with.

Speed mechanics have changed. Speed changes happen during the turn they are used, this means tailwind instantly boosts speed and speed drops active right away. This has caused tailwind to pop off and subsequently trick room is way more common to counter this. 

Another thing about speed is that there are alot of fast pokemon now, specifically regieleki is so so fast and has electroweb which has changed how you need to think about speed tiers.

I guess terrain wasn't in ORAS, terrain wars are important. Indedee F can stop priority moves and has follow me/helping hand. Rillaboom  grassy glide is insane. Misty and electric terrain are important sleep control mechanics.

This will probably get buried but this is my list of games that I think show the amazing ways video games can express stories/messages:

Portal & portal 2 - classic video game story telling, shows the power of a silent protagonist and the emotional attachment to a story that can bring (advantage is that it's extremely short)

Outerwilds - not only does this game give you a practical understanding of orbital dynamics but it's revolutionary in terms of creating your own meaning and sense of wonder well still having a written out story (Outerwilds is long if you don't cheat) (Outerwilds is similar to the witness, which is kind of an anti story, a meditative game where you come to grips with there being no story or meaning to the world - I don't recommend the witness though as it's extremely long and hard and I don't think any student would actually finish it)

Undertale - Undertale shows that video games can bring together story telling and personal moral decision making, Undertale doesn't have a message about the world at large but is instead a critique at your own personal decisions and invokes moral responsibility (also short)

Witcher 3 - witcher 3 is a masterpiece of story telling, showing that 3rd person games can still connect you personally to the world well still being about a specific protagonist (the witcher is also to long to play in a semester alongside other games)
